items.title: Manual compaction has distinct reveal and dispatch behavior
items.statement: ATS-017 requires hover to expose usage details, user selection of Compact Now before cmd.chat.compact_context dispatch, direct GUI-click coverage, /compact parity, and a prohibition on hover-only dispatch.

evidence.exact_quote: - Tests prove context-circle click does not dispatch until the user chooses Compact Now.
- Do not dispatch compaction from hover alone.

items.title: Compaction result and event states are acceptance inputs
items.statement: The acceptance surface explicitly covers started, completed, failed or visible degraded failure, plus already_running, cancelled, no_op, degraded, unavailable, retry_scheduled, completed, and failed command results.

evidence.exact_quote: - Tests cover already_running, cancelled, no_op, degraded, unavailable, retry_scheduled, completed, and failed result states.
- Failure/degraded compaction produces a visible user-facing state and event contract.

items.title: Manual compaction preserves storage lineage
items.statement: Manual Compact Now alone must not create new cache lineage unless logical run lineage changes, and Prompt Pipeline compaction_immune handling is within the acceptance scope.

evidence.exact_quote: - Manual Compact Now does not create a new cache lineage unless logical run lineage changes.

items.title: Compaction parity and recovery transition semantics are not exact
items.statement: The unit names /compact parity, equivalent visible failure/degraded state, and retry_scheduled, but does not define which click/slash outputs must be identical, the allowed equivalent event identity, or the transition and retry oracle for each listed result.
items.impact: Implementations can emit incompatible event/status mappings or claim slash parity while differing on user-visible and retry behavior.
items.builder_discretion: The builder must choose parity dimensions, equivalent degraded-event mapping, and retry transition assertions.

evidence.exact_quote: context.compaction.started, context.compaction.completed, and context.compaction.failed or equivalent visible
failure/degraded state; command-result statuses for already_running, cancelled, no_op, degraded, unavailable,

items.title: DRY defaults and non-DRY authority boundaries are fixed
items.statement: DRY is default enabled, the user may set disabled_by_user, and disabling it cannot weaken explicit instructions, safety, secret handling, source authority, governance, permissions, or source-control hygiene.

evidence.exact_quote: - DRY is default-on and user-disableable without weakening non-DRY authority boundaries.
- Do not treat disabled DRY as permission to bypass explicit instructions, safety, secrets, source authority, governance, permissions, or source-control hygiene.

items.title: One Instruction Bundle route serves all named prompt consumers
items.statement: Assistant, Interview, Orchestrator, delegated child-run, document-builder, and code-generation prompt routes must consume one shared Instruction Bundle, without prompt-builder-local DRY duplication.

evidence.exact_quote: - All prompt routes consume one shared Instruction Bundle route.
- Do not duplicate DRY prose into prompt builders.

items.title: DRY settings command, values, and explanatory copy are exact
items.statement: The Settings fixture must prove cmd.settings.agent_rules.dry_method_default_guard.set writes only enabled or disabled_by_user and displays the preserved exact help sentence.

evidence.exact_quote: - The Settings command and wiring fixture proves the toggle writes only enabled or disabled_by_user and displays the exact explanatory copy.

- "DRY Method is on by default. Turning it off disables only PM's default reuse-first guard; project/user instructions, safety, secrets, source authority, governance, permissions, and source-control rules still apply."

items.title: Unresolved DRY owner/source states stay visible
items.statement: Missing, stale, or unresolved owner/source states must be visible and policy-correct; canonical or implementation-changing mutation is expected to block, ask, or produce an open item rather than silently proceed.

evidence.exact_quote: - Missing/stale/unresolved owner-source states are visible and policy-correct.

items.title: DRY receipt fields and hash contract are absent

items.impact: Independent builders can produce mutually incompatible receipts that all claim conformance.

items.title: Container failure cleanup and retention transitions are incomplete
items.statement: Cleanup/retention disposition, retain-on-failure, and blocker payloads are required concepts, but the authoritative window does not define lifecycle ordering, failure classes, cleanup retry/timeout behavior, retention expiration, terminal states, or whether an explicit blocker substitutes for which missing proof.

items.title: Container evidence and access references lack privacy controls

dimension_assessments.summary: Manual compaction, DRY routing, container-host testing, and onboarding behaviors are explicitly enumerated.
Shared prompt routing, container discovery/probe/launch, and GUI acceptance capabilities are named.
Named statuses, commands, TestRunReceipt data, and onboarding state establish inputs/outputs, but exact receipt and state schemas are incomplete.
Several strong contracts exist, but DRY receipts, host alternatives, onboarding state, parity, and recovery mappings lack exact schemas.
Compaction, DRY, container, and onboarding states are named, while retry, cleanup/retention, and transient recovery transitions remain incomplete.
Non-DRY authority boundaries and owner-readiness proof are explicit and cannot be weakened by user-visible convenience states.
Owner docs, owner hints, source lineage, and implementation surfaces identify planning and implementation ownership.
Prompt routes, GUI/Doctor surfaces, container adapters, dependencies, and downstream unblocks identify consumers.
Compaction, DRY Settings, onboarding, Teacher, and Doctor GUI truth is substantial, but the ordered four-screen oracle is absent from this window.
Visible degraded states and fail-closed rules are specified, but deterministic recovery, cleanup, retry, and retention transitions are not.
DRY authority and onboarding sensitive-data exclusions are explicit, but container access, log, visual, and retained evidence protections are absent.
Dependencies, downstream unblocks, shared routes, owner hints, compile boundaries, and compatibility constraints express propagation.
Preflight, launch, evidence, cleanup, and retention are operationally named, but lifecycle policy, quotas, and timeouts are unresolved.
No measurable concurrency, quota, latency, timeout, or evidence-volume contract is supplied for containerized previews, stacks, or E2E runs.
Stale owners and shadow prose remain non-authoritative, Compose is not exclusive, and backend container IDs cannot define ATS truth.
The units enumerate many direct oracles, but missing receipt schemas, screen sequence, and recovery mappings prevent fully deterministic acceptance.
Fixture framework choice is intentionally open, but several consequential contract, recovery, privacy, and scale choices are also left to builders.
Material unknowns remain in parity, DRY receipt/policy, container schema/lifecycle/security/scale, and onboarding schema/recovery.
